subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Sino-Soviet split deepened sharply when the USSR withdrew its advisers and aid from China in which year?
questions.explain: The Soviet Union withdrew its technical experts and aid in 1960, signalling the open rupture.

questions.q: At the 1959 Lushan Conference, which defence minister was purged after criticising the Great Leap Forward?
questions.explain: Peng Dehuai was dismissed in 1959 after privately criticising the Great Leap Forward to Mao.

questions.q: The Tangshan earthquake, a catastrophic disaster in the final months of Mao's life, struck in which year?
questions.explain: The Tangshan earthquake of July 1976 killed hundreds of thousands and was seen by some as an omen before Mao's death.

questions.q: Premier Zhou Enlai, a moderating influence in Mao's government, died in which year, shortly before Mao?
questions.explain: Zhou Enlai died in January 1976, months before Mao's own death.

questions.q: The Great Leap Forward, Mao's drive for rapid collectivisation and industrialisation, was launched in which year?
questions.explain: The Great Leap Forward began in 1958, organising peasants into vast people's communes.

questions.q: Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China in which year?
questions.explain: Mao proclaimed the PRC from Tiananmen Square on 1 October 1949 after the Communist victory in the civil war.

questions.q: The compilation of Mao's quotations distributed to promote his cult was popularly known as what?
questions.explain: The 'Little Red Book' of Mao's quotations, edited by Lin Biao, became central to the cult of Mao.

questions.q: Who emerged as Mao's immediate successor as Chairman in 1976, famously arresting the Gang of Four?
questions.explain: Hua Guofeng succeeded Mao and ordered the arrest of the Gang of Four in October 1976.

questions.q: In which city did Mao proclaim the establishment of the People's Republic of China?
questions.explain: Mao made the proclamation from the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing on 1 October 1949.

questions.q: The Anti-Rightist Campaign of 1957 was launched in response to what?
options: The criticism unleashed during the Hundred Flowers Campaign
questions.explain: After critics spoke out during the Hundred Flowers period, Mao turned on them in the 1957 Anti-Rightist Campaign.

questions.q: Following the Communist victory, where did Chiang Kai-shek and the Nationalist (Guomindang) government retreat in 1949?
questions.explain: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists fled to Taiwan in 1949, establishing a rival government there.

questions.q: US President Richard Nixon made his historic visit to China, marking a thaw in relations, in which year?
questions.explain: Nixon visited China in February 1972, beginning the normalisation of US-China relations.

questions.q: Mao Zedong died in which year, bringing his era to an end?
questions.explain: Mao Zedong died on 9 September 1976.

questions.q: In which year did the People's Republic of China take over China's seat at the United Nations from Taiwan?
questions.explain: The PRC replaced Taiwan in the UN, including the Security Council seat, in 1971.

questions.q: The 'Three-Anti' and 'Five-Anti' campaigns of the early 1950s targeted whom?
options: Corruption among officials and the urban bourgeoisie
questions.explain: The 1951-52 campaigns attacked corruption, waste and bureaucracy among officials and capitalist businessmen.

questions.q: Who succeeded Mao as head of state and, with Deng Xiaoping, led pragmatic recovery after the Great Leap famine?
questions.explain: Liu Shaoqi became head of state in 1959 and, with Deng Xiaoping, implemented economic recovery measures.

questions.q: Which figure was named Mao's designated successor before dying in a plane crash in 1971?
questions.explain: Lin Biao, named Mao's successor in 1969, died in a plane crash in Mongolia in 1971 after an alleged failed coup.

questions.q: The 1950 Marriage Law in the PRC is significant for doing what for women?
options: Outlawing arranged marriage and granting the right to divorce
questions.explain: The 1950 Marriage Law banned arranged marriages and concubinage and gave women the right to divorce.

questions.q: The 1950 Agrarian Reform Law in the PRC primarily aimed to do what?
options: Redistribute land from landlords to poor peasants
questions.explain: The 1950 land reform redistributed land from landlords to peasants, often through violent 'struggle' campaigns.

questions.q: The 'Gang of Four', the radical clique influential in the late Cultural Revolution, was led by which of Mao's associates?
questions.explain: Jiang Qing, Mao's wife, led the Gang of Four alongside Zhang Chunqiao, Yao Wenyuan and Wang Hongwen.

questions.q: A notorious feature of the Great Leap Forward was the attempt to boost steel output through what?
questions.explain: Peasants built small 'backyard furnaces' to produce steel, much of which proved useless.

questions.q: Liu Shaoqi, branded 'China's Khrushchev', was purged and died in detention during which upheaval?
questions.explain: Liu Shaoqi was denounced and purged during the Cultural Revolution and died in prison in 1969.

questions.q: The Cultural Revolution, Mao's campaign to renew revolutionary fervour, was launched in which year?
questions.explain: The Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution was launched in 1966.

questions.q: The famine resulting from the Great Leap Forward, one of the deadliest in history, occurred mainly over which period?
questions.explain: The famine spanned roughly 1959-1962, causing tens of millions of deaths.

questions.q: Which slogan was used to describe women's contribution and equality under Mao?
options: Women hold up half the sky
questions.explain: 'Women hold up half the sky' became a slogan symbolising the official promotion of female equality.

questions.q: The Hundred Flowers Campaign, encouraging intellectuals to voice criticism, mainly took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Hundred Flowers Campaign reached its height in 1957 before being abruptly reversed.

questions.q: The radical youth mobilised to attack the 'Four Olds' during the Cultural Revolution were known as what?
questions.explain: The Red Guards, mainly students, attacked the 'Four Olds' (old ideas, culture, customs, habits) from 1966.

questions.q: The First Five-Year Plan, which prioritised heavy industry on the Soviet model, ran over which period?
questions.explain: The First Five-Year Plan ran from 1953 to 1957 and emphasised Soviet-style heavy industrialisation.

questions.q: During the Great Leap Forward, peasants were organised into what new large-scale collective units?
questions.explain: The Great Leap Forward grouped peasants into huge people's communes from 1958.

questions.q: China intervened in the Korean War in support of North Korea in which year?
questions.explain: Chinese 'People's Volunteers' entered the Korean War in October 1950 after UN forces approached the Yalu River.
